Widget API Overview

This page describes the design philosophy behind the widget API rather than its exact syntax, which is covered in the quick examples sidebar and the full reference elsewhere. The API was designed around a single principle: every widget should be constructible from a single function call, with all optional behavior expressed through plain configuration values instead of subclassing or callback registration. That principle has held up well across three major versions of the library, even as the number of supported widget types has grown from four to over thirty.

Internally the API is implemented as a thin layer over a lower-level rendering engine that most application code never touches directly. The separation exists mainly to keep the public surface small and stable, since the rendering engine has changed its internal representation twice since the project started, without requiring any changes to code written against the public widget API. Application authors who need to bypass the widget layer entirely can still reach the rendering engine directly, but that path is intentionally undocumented and unsupported.

widget.new("g", timeout=5)

The example above shows the one case where a caller needs an option beyond the default: a longer timeout for a widget whose data source is known to be slow. Every other option follows the same keyword-argument pattern, so a caller who has read this single example has effectively learned the whole surface area of the configuration system.
